dispositions.reason: Native object is dihydromethysticin, C15H16O5, with CHEBI1034670/PubChem229852. It is not the pterin substrate of FolM. No exactMatch or obsolete-ID replacement is inferred. Independently resolved FolM substrate is CHEBI71175, C9H13N5O4.

dispositions.decision: exclude asserted reaction and all connecting edges
dispositions.reason: MetaCyc pathway explicitly flags the reaction hypothetical. Rhea34844 supplies a net equation, not primary validation of an enzyme, intermediates or phosphate-release mechanism. No inspected later study resolves it.

dispositions.decision: reject prose oxidation word for terminal reaction
dispositions.reason: Primary FolM experiments and Rhea34848 establish NADPH-dependent reduction.
1997 PMID9182560 suggested a hexamer from apparent hydrodynamic mass; 1998 PMID9651328 and 1999 PMID10378270 support octamer, as do current UniProt and both native assembly objects.
UniProt wording about two pentamers of five dimers is not multiplied into20 subunits. Exact native coefficient10 and PMID12297008 pentamer-of-five-dimers evidence govern.
Issuing ChEBI SMILES fixes the monapterin side-chain stereo but leaves ringC6 unspecified. No6S identity is invented.

texts.value: Cofactor biosynthesis; 7,8-dihydroneopterin triphosphate biosynthesis; 7,8-dihydroneopterin triphosphate from GTP: step 1/1
Toroid-shaped homodecamer, composed of two pentamers of five dimers

Catalyzes the epimerization of carbon 2' of the side chain of 7,8-dihydroneopterin triphosphate (H2NTP) to form 7,8-dihydromonapterin triphosphate (H2MTP) (PubMed:9182560, PubMed:9651328). Is required for tetrahydromonapterin biosynthesis, a major pterin in E.coli (PubMed:19897652)
Catalyzes the reduction of dihydromonapterin to tetrahydromonapterin. Also has lower activity with dihydrofolate
